title: Employee copying company files before departure
description: A member of the sales team resigned and, in the days before the last working day, accessed a large number of pricing and customer files. The investigation aims to establish whether files were copied to a removable drive or to a personal online account.

sources.label: Employee laptop L-207
sources.description: Company laptop assigned to the departing employee.

sources.label: USB drive 16 GB
sources.description: Removable drive found in the employee's desk drawer.

sources.label: Corporate cloud storage account
sources.description: Company file-sharing account used by the sales team.

evidence.title: Disk image of laptop L-207
evidence.description: Forensic image of the laptop's internal drive, taken after the laptop was returned to the IT desk.
evidence.text: Image acquired through a hardware write blocker. NTFS volume 238 GB. Last user logon 2026-08-14 17:58.
custody: Handed over for file system analysis

findings: Shortcuts to files on a removable drive
Recent file shortcuts point to documents on drive letter E:, a drive that is not present on the laptop. This is consistent with files being opened from or saved to a removable drive.
medium
Compressed archive created in the user's folder
A file named q3_pricing_pack.zip was created on 2026-08-14 at 18:07 and deleted four minutes later. The deleted file was recovered from unallocated space.
high

evidence.title: USB device history from laptop registry
evidence.description: Registry export listing external storage devices that were connected to the laptop, with first and last connection times.
evidence.text: USBSTOR/Disk&Ven_Generic&Prod_Flash_Drive/4471-9A  FirstInstall=2026-08-14 18:02:19  LastConnected=2026-08-14 18:44:03  FriendlyName=Generic Flash Drive USB Device

analyses.notes: Device list comparison with the drive found in the desk.
findings: Drive serial matches the drive found in the desk
The serial 4471-9A in the registry is the same as the serial printed on the drive recovered from the employee's desk drawer, so that drive was connected to this laptop.
high

evidence.title: File access audit log for the shared sales folder
evidence.description: File server audit records for the employee's account on the shared sales folder during the two days before departure.
evidence.text:
2026-08-14 18:05:11 read user=CORP/m.fischer path=//fs01/sales/Q3_pricing/price_list_v7.xlsx
2026-08-14 18:05:12 read user=CORP/m.fischer path=//fs01/sales/Q3_pricing/discount_matrix.xlsx
2026-08-14 18:05:13 read user=CORP/m.fischer path=//fs01/sales/customers/top_accounts_2026.xlsx
Summary: 4,812 file reads between 18:05 and 18:41.

analyses.notes: Read volume and timing against normal activity.
findings: Burst of nearly five thousand file reads in 36 minutes
The account read 4,812 files in about 36 minutes after normal working hours. The employee's normal daily average is a few dozen files.
high
Activity matches the time the USB drive was connected
The read burst starts three minutes after the USB drive was first connected to the laptop and ends before it was disconnected.
high

evidence.title: Forensic image of the USB drive
evidence.description: Forensic image of the 16 GB USB drive recovered from the employee's desk.
evidence.text: FAT32 volume. Top-level folders: Q3_pricing, top_accounts, personal_photos. 1,903 files, 6.2 GB used.

findings: Company pricing and customer files on the drive
The drive holds pricing spreadsheets and a customer account list that match files in the shared sales folder by name and size.
high
Files copied on the evening of 2026-08-14
File creation times on the drive fall between 18:05 and 18:41 on 2026-08-14, matching the audit log read burst.
high

evidence.title: Cloud storage audit log for the employee account
evidence.description: Sharing and download events for the employee's account in the company cloud storage.
evidence.text:
2026-08-13 16:20:44 share_link_created user=m.fischer item=Q3_pricing audience=anyone_with_link expires=never
2026-08-14 18:50:12 download user=m.fischer item=Q3_pricing.zip size=214 MB

findings: Public link created for the pricing folder
A link that works for anyone who has it and never expires was created for the pricing folder one day before the file read burst. Whether anyone outside the company opened it is not shown in this log.
high
Large archive downloaded after hours
A 214 MB archive of the pricing folder was downloaded at 18:50, after the USB drive was disconnected.
medium

evidence.title: Resignation email to the line manager
evidence.description: Raw message in which the employee gave notice, with full headers.
evidence.text:
From: m.fischer@corp.example
To: line.manager@corp.example
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:30 +0000
Subject: Notice of resignation
I will leave on 14 August and will complete the handover of my accounts before then.

evidence.title: HR exit checklist for the employee
evidence.description: The HR checklist completed during the employee's last day.
evidence.text: Laptop returned: yes. Badge returned: yes. Cloud access removed: 2026-08-14 19:30. Removable media declared: none.

findings: Employee declared no removable media
The checklist records that no removable media was declared, although a USB drive was connected to the laptop on the employee's last day.
medium

evidence.title: Chat export with a colleague about taking files home
evidence.description: Messages between the employee and a colleague in the company chat tool on 2026-08-13.
evidence.text:
[15:41] colleague: Are you handing over the pricing sheets?
[15:44] m.fischer: I will keep a copy for my own reference, nothing sensitive.
[15:45] colleague: Ok, just check with the manager first.
evidence.notes: Colleague's name removed from the export.

evidence.title: Browser history showing a personal webmail and file transfer site
evidence.description: Web history from the employee's browser profile on the laptop for the last three days.

findings: Visit to a file upload service after the download
The browser visited an upload service about five minutes after the cloud archive was downloaded and reached a completion page. The content of the upload is not recorded in the history.
medium

evidence.title: Screenshot of the USB drive folder properties
evidence.description: Screenshot of the folder properties dialog for the pricing folder on the USB drive.

findings: Screenshot shows folder size and file count
The dialog shows 1,203 files and 4.4 GB in the pricing folder, which matches the count from the forensic image of the drive.
info

evidence.title: Endpoint data loss prevention alert log
evidence.description: Alerts raised by the endpoint protection agent on the laptop on the employee's last day.
evidence.text:
2026-08-14 18:06:44 alert policy=removable_media_write severity=medium user=m.fischer action=logged
2026-08-14 18:06:45 alert policy=bulk_file_read severity=high user=m.fischer action=logged

findings: Alerts were logged but not blocked
Both alerts were set to log only, so the protection agent recorded the activity without stopping it or notifying anyone.
low

evidence.title: Truncated duplicate of the file access audit log
evidence.description: A second export of the file access audit log that covers only half of the time range of the main export.
evidence.notes: Export was cut off by a time limit on the server.

withdrawn.reason: Duplicate of the complete export and covers only half the time range.

links: The serial 4471-9A in the registry history matches the serial of the drive imaged as evidence 4.
File read times on the server match the creation times of the files found on the USB drive.
The pricing folder on the USB drive matches the archive recovered from unallocated space on the laptop.
The resignation notice and the sharing and download activity in the cloud account fall in the same last week.
The checklist says no removable media was declared, but the registry shows a drive was connected on the last day.
